radiology_report:
Erasmus MC
Department of Radiology
Date: 12 Dec 2024
Exam: mpMRI Prostate (1.5T)

Clinical indication: Rising PSA (6.9 ng/mL) and prior biopsy-proven adenocarcinoma. Request for staging and lesion characterization.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume is calculated at 57.4 mL. The peripheral zone is unremarkable except for a focal lesion in the right paramedian apex, extending into the transition zone. On T2-weighted imaging, this area demonstrates low signal intensity with irregular margins. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows marked restricted diffusion with high signal on b=1400 and corresponding low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences reveal early, intense, and rapid wash-in of contrast within the same region, confirming high vascularity. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or distant metastases are seen.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right paramedian apex/transition zone, approximately 14 mm in maximal dimension.
PSA density: 0.12 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cT1c.
csPCa predicted probability 0.84531116.

previous_notes.author: Dr. M. Jansen (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with elevated PSA of 2.0 ng/mL, up from 1.3 ng/mL in November 2022. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable. Discussed the rising trend and arranged for repeat PSA in six months to assess velocity. Advised on lifestyle factors and continued monitoring of his diabetes and cardiac health.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1 (2024): The submitted tissue sections demonstrate acinar adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 4+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 4. A cribriform pattern is present within the tumor architecture. Perineural invasion is identified. The tumor is located in the transition zone, specifically at the paramedian apex right. The histological findings indicate a high-grade disease with aggressive features.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 3.
